+# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):

+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"

    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""

    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"

    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi

    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}

    75	_loa_pl_id() {

    84	}

    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out

    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi

    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;

    78	set -euo pipefail
    79	export LC_ALL=C
    80	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    82	usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    83	
    84	sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
    85	file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
    86	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    87	  case "$1" in
    88	    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    89	    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    90	    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    91	    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    92	    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    93	    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    94	    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    95	    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    96	    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;

   102	
   103	# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
   104	# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
   105	# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
   106	if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
   107	  run_dir="$root/.run"
   108	else
   109	  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
   110	  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
   111	  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
   112	    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
   113	    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
   114	  fi
   115	fi
   116	if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi

   118	[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
   119	CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"
   120	
   121	now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
   122	
   123	# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
   124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
   125	cfg() {
   126	  local v
   127	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
   128	    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
   129	    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
   130	  else
   131	    printf 'null'
   132	  fi
   133	}
   134	cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
   135	  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
   136	  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
   137	}
   138	
   139	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
   140	
   141	# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
   142	# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
   143	# previous file is untouched.
   144	atomic_update() {
   145	  local f="$1"; shift
   146	  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
   147	  (
   148	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
   149	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
   150	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
   151	    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
   152	      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
   153	    else
   154	      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
   155	    fi
   156	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
   157	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
   158	  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
   159	  return $rc
   160	}
   161	
   162	cmd_write() {
   163	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
   164	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
   165	  local ts rc=0
   166	  ts=$(now_iso)
   167	  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
   168	    '.schema_version = 2
   169	     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
   170	     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
   171	  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
   172	  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
   173	  local err drc=0
   174	  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
   175	  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
   176	  return 0
   177	}
   178	
   179	bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
   180	  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
   181	  local js st
   182	  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   183	  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   184	  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
   185	}
   186	
   187	cmd_read() {
   188	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
   189	  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
   190	  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
   191	  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
   192	  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
   193	  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
   194	    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
   195	    return 0
   196	  fi
   197	  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")

   199	  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
   200	    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
   201	    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
   202	    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
   203	    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
   204	  fi
   205	  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
   206	    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
   207	    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
   208	    return 0
   209	  fi
   210	  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
   211	  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
   212	}
   213	
   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}
   241	
   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}
   250	
   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}
   271	
   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr

   123	# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
   124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
   125	cfg() {
   126	  local v
   127	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
   128	    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
   129	    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
   130	  else
   131	    printf 'null'
   132	  fi

   134	cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
   135	  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
   136	  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi

   139	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

   141	# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
   142	# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
   143	# previous file is untouched.
   144	atomic_update() {
   145	  local f="$1"; shift
   146	  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
   147	  (
   148	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
   149	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
   150	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
   151	    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
   152	      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
   153	    else
   154	      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
   155	    fi
   156	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
   157	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
   158	  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
   159	  return $rc
   160	}

   162	cmd_write() {
   163	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
   164	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi

   166	  ts=$(now_iso)
   167	  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
   168	    '.schema_version = 2
   169	     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
   170	     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
   171	  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
   172	  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
   173	  local err drc=0
   174	  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?

   179	bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
   180	  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
   181	  local js st
   182	  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   183	  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   184	  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]

   187	cmd_read() {
   188	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi

   191	  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
   192	  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
   193	  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
   194	    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi

   196	  fi
   197	  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")

   199	  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
   200	    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
   201	    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
   202	    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
   203	    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
   204	  fi
   205	  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
   206	    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
   207	    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
   208	    return 0
   209	  fi
   210	  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
   211	  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
   212	}

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}
   241	
   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}

   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}

   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr

280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr

   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):

   331	cmd_derive() {

   483	  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")

   488	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
   489	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \

   493	  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
   494	  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
   495	      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   496	    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   497	    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
   498	    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
   499	       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
   500	       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
   501	    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
   502	       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
   503	       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
   504	    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
   505	    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
   506	    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
   507	    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)

   511	        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   512	          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
   513	        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
   514	          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]

   517	    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
   518	    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"

   529	    return 10
   530	  fi
   531	  return 0
   532	}

     2	# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
     3	# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
     4	# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
     5	# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
     6	# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-corpus.sh — replay tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl through the
# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
#
# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]
# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0
#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2
#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
# --knob-off  writes destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false into the
#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);
#             compare it with the pre-change hook through --rows.
# --rows      prints "<id> <exit code>" per row instead of the summary (for diffs).
# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then
#   "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N p95_ms M";
# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
set -uo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
if (( knob_off )); then
  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
fi

bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
mismatches=()
durations=()
# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
now_us() {
  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
  else
    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
  fi
}
start_us=$(now_us)
while IFS= read -r row; do
  [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
  id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row"); expect=$(jq -r '.expect' <<<"$row")
  cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // "repo"' <<<"$row"); tmpdir=$(jq -r '.env.TMPDIR // empty' <<<"$row")
  dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"
  payload=$(jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}')
  rc=0
  t0=$(now_us)
  if [[ -n "$tmpdir" ]]; then
    (cd "$dir" && TMPDIR="$tmpdir" bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
  else
    (cd "$dir" && env -u TMPDIR bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
  fi
  t1=$(now_us)
  durations+=("$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000 ))")
  (( rows_out )) && printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$rc"
  case "$expect" in
    allow)    bt=$((bt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then bp=$((bp+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-allow:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    block)    dt=$((dt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then db=$((db+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-block:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    residual) rt=$((rt+1)); [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && rp=$((rp+1)) ;;
    *) mismatches+=("$id:unknown-expect:$expect") ;;
  esac
done < "$corpus"
end_us=$(now_us)
runtime=$(( (end_us - start_us) / 1000 ))
n=${#durations[@]}
p95=0
if (( n > 0 )); then
  idx=$(( (n * 95 + 99) / 100 ))      # nearest-rank: ceil(0.95 n)
  p95=$(printf '%s\n' "${durations[@]}" | sort -n | sed -n "${idx}p")
fi

(( rows_out )) && exit 0
if (( json )); then
  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson bp "$bp" --argjson bt "$bt" --argjson db "$db" --argjson dt "$dt" \
    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" --argjson p95 "$p95" --argjson n "$n" \
    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, p95_ms:$p95, rows:$n, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
else
  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | sed '/^$/d'
  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime p95_ms $p95"
fi

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. 2	# =============================================================================
3	# PreToolUse:Bash Safety Hook — Block Destructive Commands (v1.38.0)
4	# =============================================================================
5	# Blocks dangerous patterns and suggests safer alternatives.
6	# Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block (stderr message fed back to agent).
7	#
8	# Cycle-111 (sprint-164, 2026-05-16) — ports Anthropic DCG public pattern
9	# set inline. Source: github.com/anthropics/destructive-command-guard
10	# Pattern port reference SHA: HEAD as of 2026-05-16 (no specific commit
11	# pin available — DCG ships rule packs, not single-file source).
12	# REVIEW-BY: 2026-08-16 — re-sync against upstream DCG every quarter.
13	#
14	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
15	# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
16	#
17	# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
18	# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
19	# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
20	# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
21	# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
22	# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
23	#
24	# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
25	# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
26	# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
27	# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
28	# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
29	# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
30	#
31	# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
32	# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
33	# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
34	# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
35	#
36	# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
37	# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
38	# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
39	# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
40	# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
41	# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
42	# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
43	# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
44	#
45	# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
46	# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
47	# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
48	# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
49	# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
50	# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
51	# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
52	# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
53	# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
54	# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
55	# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
56	#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
57	#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote
58	#     payloads was withdrawn at design time (Flatline SKP-001) — the text
59	#     fence cannot tell a remote target from a local one, and the blast
60	#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
61	#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
62	#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
63	#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
64	#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
65	#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
66	#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
67	#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
68	#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
69	#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
70	#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
71	#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
72	#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
73	#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
74	#
75	# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
76	# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
77	# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
78	# =============================================================================
79	# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
80	# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
81	# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
82	# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
83	# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
84	# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
85	# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
86	# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
87	# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
88	# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
89	# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
90	# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
91	# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
92	# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
93	# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
94	# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
95	# =============================================================================
96	# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
97	# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
98	# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
99	# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
100	# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
101	# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
102	# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
103	# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
104	# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
105	# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
106	# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
107	# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
108	# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
109	# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
110	# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
111	# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
112	# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
113	# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
114	# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
115	# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
116	# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
117	# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
118	# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
119	# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
120	# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
121	# =============================================================================
122	
123	# =============================================================================
124	# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
125	# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
126	# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
127	# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
128	# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
129	#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
130	#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
131	# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
132	# under a caller's `set -u`.
133	#
134	# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
135	# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
136	# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
137	# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
138	# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
139	# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
140	# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
141	# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
142	# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
143	#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
144	#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
145	#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
146	#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
147	#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
148	#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
149	#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
150	#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
151	#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
152	#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
153	#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
154	#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
155	#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
156	#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
157	#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
158	#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
159	#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
160	#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
161	#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
162	#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
163	#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,

229	# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
230	# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
231	# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
232	_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
233	  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
234	  n=${#s}
235	  _bdb_hd_tok=()
236	  while (( i < n )); do
237	    ch="${s:i:1}"
238	    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
239	      tok="$tok$ch"
240	      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
241	        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
242	      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
243	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
244	        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
245	      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
246	        q=""
247	      fi
248	      i=$((i + 1)); continue
249	    fi
250	    case "$ch" in
251	      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
252	      '\')
253	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
254	        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
255	      ' '|$'\t')
256	        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
257	        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
258	      '#')
259	        (( have )) || return 1
260	        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
261	      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
262	        op=""
263	        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
264	          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
265	        done
266	        i=$((i + ${#op}))
267	        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
268	          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
269	        fi
270	        if (( have )); then
271	          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
272	            op="$tok$op"
273	          else
274	            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
275	          fi
276	          tok=""; have=0
277	        fi
278	        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
279	      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
280	    esac
281	  done
282	  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
283	  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
284	  return 0
285	}

287	# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
288	# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
289	_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
290	  _hd_up=""
291	  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
292	    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
293	  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
294	    _hd_up="$1"
295	  else
296	    return 1
297	  fi
298	  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
299	}

301	# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
302	# content (or cannot be judged).
303	_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
304	  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
305	  case "$p" in
306	    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
307	  esac
308	  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
309	  b="${p##*/}"
310	  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
311	  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
312	  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
313	  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
314	  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
315	  else d="${PWD:-.}"
316	  fi
317	  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
318	  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
319	    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
320	    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
321	    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
322	  done
323	  IFS="$old_ifs"
324	  return 1
325	}

327	# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
328	# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
329	_bdb_hd_member() {
330	  local -a toks argv
331	  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
332	  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
333	  _hd_mcls=none
334	  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
335	    t="${toks[i]}"
336	    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
337	      case "$t" in
338	        *'<<<') return ;;
339	        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
340	        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
341	        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
342	          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
343	          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
344	          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
345	          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
346	          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
347	          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
348	          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
349	          continue ;;
350	        *) return ;;
351	      esac
352	    fi
353	    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
354	  done
355	  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
356	  a0="${argv[0]}"
357	  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
358	  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
359	  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
360	  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
361	  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
362	    t="${argv[i]}"
363	    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
364	  done
365	  case "$a0" in
366	    cat)
367	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
368	    tee)
369	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
370	        t="${argv[i]}"
371	        case "$t" in
372	          -a|--append|-p) ;;
373	          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
374	          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
375	             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
376	        esac
377	      done ;;
378	    echo|printf)
379	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
380	        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
381	      done ;;
382	    gh)
383	      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
384	        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
385	        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
386	        *) return ;;
387	      esac
388	      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
389	        t="${argv[i]}"
390	        case "$t" in
391	          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
392	          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
393	          -*)
394	            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
395	              i=$((i + 1))
396	              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
397	            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
398	              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
399	            fi ;;
400	          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
401	        esac
402	      done
403	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
404	    git)
405	      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
406	      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
407	        t="${argv[i]}"
408	        case "$t" in
409	          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
410	          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
411	          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
412	          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
413	        esac
414	      done
415	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
416	    br)
417	      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
418	      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
419	        t="${argv[i]}"
420	        case "$t" in
421	          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
422	          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
423	          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
424	        esac
425	      done
426	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
427	    jq|yq)
428	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
429	        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
430	        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
431	        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
432	      done ;;
433	    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
434	    sed)
435	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
436	        t="${argv[i]}"
437	        case "$t" in
438	          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
439	          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
440	          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
441	          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
442	               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
443	               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
444	             fi ;;
445	        esac
446	      done
447	      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
448	    sort)
449	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
450	        t="${argv[i]}"
451	        case "$t" in
452	          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
453	          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
454	          -k*|-t*) ;;
455	          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
456	          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
457	        esac
458	      done ;;
459	    wc)
460	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
461	        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
462	      done ;;
463	    *) return ;;
464	  esac
465	  _hd_mcls=nonexec
466	}

468	# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
469	# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
470	# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
471	_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
472	  local l="${1:-}" k last
473	  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
474	  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
475	  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
476	    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
477	      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
478	    esac
479	  done
480	  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
481	  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
482	  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
483	  return 1
484	}

486	# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
487	# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
488	# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
489	_bdb_hd_header() {
490	  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
491	  local -a tpipe mtoks
492	  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
493	  _hd_dests=()
494	  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
495	  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
496	  tpipe=()
497	  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
498	    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
499	    case "$t" in
500	      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
501	      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
502	    esac
503	    tpipe[k]=$pipe
504	    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
505	  done
506	  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
507	  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
508	  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
509	  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
510	    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
511	  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
512	    _hd_delim="$w"
513	  else
514	    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
515	  fi
516	  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
517	  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
518	  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
519	  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
520	  local cls=nonexec
521	  k=0
522	  while (( k < nt )); do
523	    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
524	    mtoks=()
525	    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
526	    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
527	    case "$_hd_mcls" in
528	      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
529	      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
530	    esac
531	    k=$((k + 1))
532	  done
533	  _hd_cls="$cls"
534	}

536	# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
537	# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
538	_bdb_hd_segword() {
539	  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
540	  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
541	  while (( guard < 64 )); do
542	    guard=$((guard + 1))
543	    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
544	    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
545	    case "${s:0:1}" in
546	      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
547	    esac
548	    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
549	    s="${s:${#w}}"
550	    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
551	    case "$w" in
552	      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
553	        while :; do
554	          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
555	          case "$s" in
556	            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
557	            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
558	              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
559	            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
560	            *) break ;;
561	          esac
562	        done
563	        continue ;;
564	    esac
565	    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
566	    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
567	    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
568	    return
569	  done
570	}

572	# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
573	# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
574	# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
575	# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
576	_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
577	  local k l t seg
578	  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
579	  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
580	    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"

606	# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe

608	_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {

610	  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
611	    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue

641	# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
  else
    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
  fi
}

# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
_loa_pl_id() {
  local st
  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    return 0
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
}

_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
_loa_pl_build() {
  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
        else . end)) as $knobs |
    {
      schema_version: 1,
      id: $id,
      profile: $sel.name,
      profile_source: $sel.source,
      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
      profile_keys: $keys,
      knobs: $knobs,
      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
  local w
  while IFS= read -r w; do
    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
  return 0
}

_loa_pl_write_cache() {
  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  fi
  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  return 0
}

# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
_loa_pl_load() {
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
    local j
    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  _loa_pl_build || return 1
  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
