#!/usr/bin/env bash
# validate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry validator
# Runs 8 validation checks against constraints.json + generated sections
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/compat-lib.sh"

# Constants
readonly REGISTRY=".claude/data/constraints.json"
readonly SCHEMA=".claude/schemas/constraints.schema.json"
readonly TEMPLATE_DIR=".claude/templates/constraints"
readonly GENERATE_SCRIPT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/generate-constraints.sh"

# Section definitions (duplicated from generate-constraints.sh for freshness check)
readonly -a SECTIONS=(
  "process_compliance_never|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_never\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "process_compliance_always|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_always\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|task-tracking.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"task_tracking_hierarchy\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|.claude/protocols/implementation-compliance.md|protocol-checklist.jq|[\"C-PROC-008\",\"C-PROC-006\",\"C-PROC-009\",\"C-PROC-010\",\"C-GIT-001\",\"C-PROC-005\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "autonomous_agent_constraints|.claude/skills/autonomous-agent/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PHASE-001\",\"C-PHASE-003\",\"C-PHASE-004\",\"C-PHASE-006\",\"C-PROC-003\",\"C-PROC-004\",\"C-PROC-002\",\"C-PROC-006\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "simstim_constraints|.claude/skills/simstim-workflow/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PHASE-002\",\"C-PHASE-003\",\"C-PHASE-004\",\"C-PHASE-007\",\"C-PHASE-008\",\"C-PROC-005\",\"C-PHASE-005\",\"C-PROC-002\",\"C-PROC-006\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "implementing_tasks_constraints|.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.target == \"skill-md\" and (.skills | index(\"implementing-tasks\"))))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "merge_constraints|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"merge_constraints\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "agent_teams_constraints|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"agent_teams_constraints\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "discovering_requirements_grants|.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PERM-001\",\"C-PERM-004\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "reviewing_code_grants|.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PERM-003\",\"C-PERM-004\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "bridgebuilder_review_grants|.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PERM-001\",\"C-PERM-003\",\"C-PERM-004\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "run_bridge_constraints|.claude/skills/run-bridge/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-BRIDGE-001\",\"C-BRIDGE-002\",\"C-BRIDGE-003\",\"C-BRIDGE-004\",\"C-BRIDGE-005\",\"C-BRIDGE-006\",\"C-BRIDGE-007\",\"C-BRIDGE-008\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
  "deploying_infrastructure_merge|.claude/skills/deploying-infrastructure/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-MERGE-003\",\"C-MERGE-004\",\"C-MERGE-005\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
)

# Counters
ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0
VERBOSE=false

# ============================================================================
# Utilities
# ============================================================================

log() { echo "[validate-constraints] $*" >&2; }
verbose() { [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && log "$@" || true; }
pass() { echo "  PASS: $*"; }
fail() { echo "  FAIL: $*"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
warn() { echo "  WARN: $*"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }

compute_section_hash() {
  printf '%s' "$1" \
    | tr -d '\r' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' \
    | sha256_portable \
    | cut -c1-16
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON
# ============================================================================

check_registry_exists() {
  log "Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON"

  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then
    fail "Registry not found: $REGISTRY"
    return 1
  fi

  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then
    fail "Registry is not valid JSON: $REGISTRY"
    return 1
  fi

  local count
  count=$(jq '.constraints | length' "$REGISTRY")
  pass "Registry is valid JSON with $count constraints"
  return 0
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 2: Schema compliance (ajv or jq fallback)
# ============================================================================

check_schema_compliance() {
  log "Check 2: Schema compliance"

  if [[ ! -f "$SCHEMA" ]]; then
    fail "Schema not found: $SCHEMA"
    return 1
  fi

  if command -v ajv &>/dev/null; then
    if ajv validate -s "$SCHEMA" -d "$REGISTRY" --spec=draft2020 2>&1; then
      pass "Schema validation passed (ajv)"
      return 0
    else
      fail "Schema validation failed (ajv)"
      return 1
    fi
  fi

  # jq fallback: check required fields, ID patterns, enums
  local errors=0

  # Check top-level required fields
  if ! jq -e '.version and .constraints' "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "Missing required top-level fields (version, constraints)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Check version pattern
  local version
  version=$(jq -r '.version' "$REGISTRY")
  if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    fail "Invalid version format: $version"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check each constraint has required fields
  local missing
  missing=$(jq -r '
    [.constraints[] | select(
      (.id | not) or (.name | not) or (.category | not) or
      (.rule_type | not) or (.text | not) or (.why | not) or
      (.layers | not) or (.severity | not)
    ) | .id // "UNKNOWN"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
    fail "Constraints missing required fields: $missing"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check ID pattern
  local bad_ids
  bad_ids=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select(.id | test("^C-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3}$") | not) | .id] | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_ids" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid constraint IDs: $bad_ids"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

# ============================================================================
# Check 3: No duplicate IDs
# ============================================================================

check_unique_ids() {
  log "Check 3: No duplicate IDs"

  local dupes
  dupes=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].id] | sort | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1)) | map(.[0]) | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$dupes" ]]; then
    fail "Duplicate constraint IDs: $dupes"
    return 1
  fi

  pass "All constraint IDs are unique"
  return 0
}

# ============================================================================
# Check 4: Error code cross-references valid
# ============================================================================

check_error_code_refs() {
  log "Check 4: Error code cross-references"

  local error_codes_file=".claude/data/error-codes.json"
  if [[ ! -f "$error_codes_file" ]]; then
    warn "Error codes file not found: $error_codes_file (skipping cross-reference check)"
    return 0
  fi

  # Get all error_code values from constraints
  local constraint_codes
  constraint_codes=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select(.error_code) | .error_code] | unique | .[]' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -z "$constraint_codes" ]]; then
    pass "No error code cross-references to validate"
    return 0

  local errors=0

  return $((errors > 0 ? 1 : 0))

compute_section_hash() {
  # SHA-256, first 16 chars, LF-normalized, trailing whitespace trimmed
  printf '%s' "$1" \
    | tr -d '\r' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' \
    | sha256_portable \
    | cut -c1-16
}

# ============================================================================
# Registry validation
# ============================================================================

validate_registry() {
  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then
    die "Registry not found: $REGISTRY"
  fi

  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then
    die "Registry is not valid JSON: $REGISTRY"
  fi

  # Check for duplicate IDs
  local dupes
  dupes=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].id] | sort | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1)) | length' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ "$dupes" -gt 0 ]]; then
    die "Registry has duplicate constraint IDs"
  fi

  verbose "Registry validated: $(jq '.constraints | length' "$REGISTRY") constraints"
}

# ============================================================================
# Rendering
# ============================================================================

render_section() {
  local section_name="$1"
  local template="$2"
  local filter_jq="$3"

  local template_file="${TEMPLATE_DIR}/${template}"
  if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
    die "Template not found: $template_file"
  fi

  jq -r "$filter_jq" "$REGISTRY" | jq -r -f "$template_file"
}

# ============================================================================
# Section insertion
# ============================================================================

insert_generated_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    # Replace content between existing markers
    local tmp="${file}.gen-tmp"
    awk -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section}" \
        -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section}" \
        -v new_start="$start_marker" \
        -v new_warning="$warning" \
        -v new_content="$content" \
        -v new_end="$end_marker" \
        '
        $0 ~ start { print new_start; print new_warning; printf "%s\n", new_content; skip=1; next }
        $0 ~ end   { print new_end; skip=0; next }
        !skip       { print }
        ' "$file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
  else
    log "ERROR: Missing markers in ${file} for section '${section}'. Run with --bootstrap --confirm to insert."
    return 1
  fi
}

# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
# is not optional.
optional_table_heading() {
  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading

  for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do
    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ -n "$SECTION_FILTER" ]] && [[ "$s_name" != "$SECTION_FILTER" ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done
  done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
      log "Diff for ${target}:"
      diff -u "$target" "${staged_files[$target]}" || true
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if mv "${staged_files[$target]}" "$target"; then
      committed+=("$target")
    else
      commit_failed=true
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ "$commit_failed" == "true" ]]; then
    local rollback_ok=true
    for t in "${committed[@]}"; do
      if ! cp -f "${backup_files[$t]}" "$t"; then
        rollback_ok=false
      fi
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    if [[ "$rollback_ok" == "true" ]]; then
      for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — all targets rolled back"
    else
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — rollback partially failed, .constraint-bak files preserved"
    fi
    trap - EXIT
    return 1
  fi

  # Success: clean up backups and update @loa-managed hashes
  for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
  trap - EXIT

  # Phase 4: Update @loa-managed hashes (IMP-002)
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if bash "$MARKER_UTILS" has-marker "$target" | grep -q "true"; then
      verbose "Updating @loa-managed hash for ${target}"
      bash "$MARKER_UTILS" update-hash "$target"
    fi

   complete. Start a new run with `/run sprint-N`." → exit 1.

   mismatch / Expected: {expected} / Current: {current} / Checkout the correct branch: `git
   checkout {expected}`" → exit 1.

   `git fetch origin "$branch" 2>&1` (never redirect stash/git diagnostic output to `/dev/null`
   per `.claude/rules/stash-safety.md`'s spirit — surface fetch failures), then compare
   `git rev-parse HEAD` against `git rev-parse "origin/$branch"`. Same → fine. If
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$branch" HEAD` succeeds (local ahead) → fine. Otherwise
   diverged: "ERROR: Branch has diverged from remote / Local: {local} / Remote: {remote} / This
   can happen if someone else pushed, or you made changes outside Run Mode. / To force resume: `/run-resume --force`.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
#
# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

# RTFM Testing Skill

<objective>
Spawn a zero-context agent to test documentation usability. The tester operates under strict "no inference" rules and reports every gap it encounters. Parse the structured gap report, determine a verdict, and write results to the RTFM report directory.

This is a hermetic documentation test — the agent equivalent of a hermetic build. No implicit dependencies, no ambient state. If the zero-context agent can't follow the docs, the docs have gaps.
</objective>

The documentation paths checked always include `docs/` (`docs/CONFIG_REFERENCE.md` and its siblings are first-class documentation artifacts) alongside any other paths in scope.

- READ: Documentation files specified by user (any path)

- WRITE: grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/ (reports and baselines)

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)

+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \

name: Prompt Budget

# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
# read as green).

on:
  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
  # PR #1266.
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prompt-budget:
    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5

      - name: Check budgets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
            cat prompt-budget.json || true
            exit 1
          fi
          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null

      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"

      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under --quiet; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh false-positive on tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: under-budget sentinel accepted"

      - name: Upload report
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: prompt-budget-report
          path: prompt-budget.json
          retention-days: 14

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"

    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
    : > "$CFG"
}

knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }

@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    for p in standard full; do
        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
}

@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
}

@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
    local k want got
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'true/false\ntrue/false')" ]
}

@test "PL-4 standard equals the post-cycle example defaults (explicit example value, else the reader's fallback)" {

        ex=$(yq -r ".$k" "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")

        fi
        [ "$ex" = "$st" ] || { echo "example $k = $ex, standard $st"; return 1; }
    done < <(yq -r '.profiles.standard | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES")
    [ "$(yq -r '.loa.profile' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")" = "standard" ]
    # Under the example config the lib resolves standard and no override.

    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: true\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 250\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]     # explicit
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback

    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"

    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]

    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]

    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"

    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]

content.text:
I found 9 issues in my scope; two are worth fixing before merge (1 and 2), the rest are low severity. The PR copy holds only the changed files (no `compat-lib.sh`, hooks, templates or unchanged skills), so I couldn't run `validate-constraints.sh`, the generator or the bats suites. The findings below come from reading the code, plus `yq` and shell probes run on a copy in `/tmp`.

**Checked and fine:**
- **Skill includes:** every changed skill's include body matches its source file (with `{{SKILL}}` filled in), and the stored hash is right. The hash is the md5 of the content without its trailing newline.
- **No leftover C-TEAM references:** apart from the agent-teams reference and the new tests, nothing in the copy still points at the removed rows or the `agent_teams_constraints` section.
- **Configs:** both YAML files parse and have no duplicate top-level keys. The `standard` values in `profiles.yaml` match the example's per-key defaults.
- **Documented defaults** for `implement_gate`, `run_mode.stale_hours` (12 h) and the two-hour marker match `implement-gate.sh` and `run-checkpoint.sh`.
- **Prompt budget:** `CLAUDE.loa.md` is 9,189 B, under the new 9,445 B cap.
- **`check-knob-readers.sh`** exits 0 on the copy (9 keys checked).

## Defects

1. **`loa.profile` does almost nothing for anyone who copies the example** — `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:32` (`loa: profile: standard`). High certainty; usability/design defect.
   - The example sets 8 of the 9 profile keys explicitly, and an explicit key always wins over the profile.
   - So a user who copies the example and switches to `lean` or `full` only changes `soul_identity_doc.enabled`.
   - Evidence from `yq`: `known_failures.surface_at_session_start`, `decisions.surface_at_session_start`, both `karpathy_principles.*`, both `guardrails.*`, `invisible_retrospective.enabled` and `structured_handoff.enabled` are all set (e.g. lines 1358, 1404). The comment at lines 24–26 admits "A key you set explicitly anywhere in this file wins".

2. **Skills outside the diff may still carry the old include text** — `head/.claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md:4` and `retrospective_postlude.md:1`. Unverified.
   - Only 6 skills got regenerated includes.
   - `tools/prompt-keeplist.txt` K-41/K-42 lists 13 skills, including planning-sprints, simstim-workflow, riding-codebase, discovering-requirements and translating-for-executives. None of those appear in the diff.
   - If any of them embeds these includes, it still has the old text and hash: the guardrails "Skip … Otherwise" wording that reads the key directly, without the profile.
   - To settle it, run the include drift check on the full tree.

3. **Lint asks for a fix the generator cannot make** — `head/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh:243-244`. High certainty.
   - The lint reports an ERROR whenever the class is empty and the `## Agent Teams` heading is present, even with no marker, and tells you to "run generate-constraints.sh".
   - But `prune_optional_table` (`generate-constraints.sh`, around line 170) returns early as a no-op when the start marker is missing.
   - A kernel left with only the heading therefore fails lint forever; regenerating never clears it.

4. **Pruning can silently succeed without pruning** — `head/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh`, awk `END` block (around lines 185–189). Medium certainty.
   - If the start marker sits above the `## Agent Teams` heading, or the heading is the last thing in the file, awk ends in state `head`.
   - It then flushes and exits 0 without exit code 3 or 4.
   - The markers stay in the file and the generator reports success.

5. **The lint self-test no longer separates "all pass" from "warnings"** — `head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257` and `:320`. High certainty.
   - Both checks now accept exit 0 or 1 via the new `assert_no_errors_exit`.
   - The test labelled "Exit code semantics" can't tell exit 0 from exit 1 any more, so a regression that turns every PASS into a WARN stays green.

6. **Run-mode prose contradicts itself on when to call `record-round`** — `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:110` vs `:131-132`. High certainty.
   - Step 5 calls `record-round` only on findings. The Circuit Breaker section says to call it after *each* review and audit.
   - That matters, because no-progress and same-issue counting depend on which rounds get recorded.
   - The phrase "exit 10, HALT; else continue" is also ambiguous: it reads as if every findings round halts.

7. **The two retrospective-postlude instructions behave differently when the profile can't resolve** — `head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` vs `head/.claude/skills/continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34`. Medium certainty, low impact.
   - The include calls `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback; the resource passes fallback `true`.
   - Without jq/yq, `loa_knob` falls back to `_loa_pl_live`, which prints the fallback, so the include prints `""` and treats the feature as disabled.
   - The resource's call prints `true`, so the same setup reads as enabled.

8. **A doc-lock test now passes on a comment** — `head/tests/unit/golden-path-c8-verdict-trailer.bats` (FR-5 doc-lock). Low severity.
   - `grep -q "verdict-derive.sh --json"` and `grep -q 'no trailer'` only match header comments in `run-checkpoint.sh` (lines 53–55).
   - The code itself calls `verdict-derive.sh --file … --gate … --json` (line 222).
   - The lock survives if the implementation changes, as long as the comment stays.

9. **The rtfm-testing docs disagree on what it writes** — `head/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md:52` vs `head/.claude/skills/rtfm-testing/SKILL.md:55`. Low severity.
   - The rule says rtfm-testing "writes one new … report per run and edits nothing".
   - The skill's zone constraints say "WRITE: grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/ (reports and baselines)".

## Lesser notes (not defects)

- **Default posture change:** `guardrails.input.enabled` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` now default to false (example lines 1358 and 1404, `profiles.yaml` `standard`). `danger-level-enforcer.sh:142` and `guardrails-orchestrator.sh:110` now fall back to `false`, where before they fell back to `true`. This is documented (DEC-0161) but turns guardrails off for new installs; this repository keeps the input guardrails on explicitly.
- **Freshness check can't catch missing markers:** `validate-constraints.sh:25` adds `agent_teams_constraints`, but its freshness check skips a section with no markers. Only `lint-invariants.sh` catches "rows exist but markers are missing", which is acceptable.

@test "PL-14 the /loa Profile line prints the profile and the explicit overrides" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE
    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')

    : > "$CFG"

  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" registry=".claude/data/constraints.json"

+# Exit 0 (all pass) or 1 (warnings only): the good fixture cannot satisfy the
+# environment-dependent invariants (live settings.json, header hash), so its
+# WARNs are expected; an ERROR (exit 2) is not.
+assert_no_errors_exit() {
+  local actual="$1"
+  local desc="$2"
+
+  TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+  if [[ "$actual" -eq 0 || "$actual" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
+    [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && printf "  [PASS] %s\n" "$desc"
+  else
+    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
+    printf "  [FAIL] %s (expected exit 0 or 1, got %d)\n" "$desc" "$actual"
+  fi
+}

   local output="$1"

@@ -237,7 +254,7 @@ parse_result "$result"

        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    else
        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    fi
}

# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
}

# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
cut_utf8_256() {
    local LC_ALL=C
    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
    _c_n=${#_c_s}
    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
        fi
        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
        return 0
    done
    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
}

# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
strip_controls() {
    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')
    (( ${#_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]} )) || _ig_strip_seqs_init
    while :; do
        prev=$s
        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
    done
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.10
# (PRD FR-5 AC-5.1 … AC-5.4, FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-5.1, D-5.1a, D-5.2, D-5.3, D-5.4)
# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/repo"
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
  git -C "$R" init -q
  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
  git -C "$R" add -A
  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
  ledger completed completed completed
  unset LOA_RUN_DIR LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
ledger() {
  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
     cycles: [
       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
}

# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
feedback() {
  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
  else
    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
  fi
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
}

# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
complete() {
  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
}

# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
cache() {
  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
dj() { jq -r "$1" <<<"$output"; }

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

content.text:
I found 11 defects in the FR-6 classifier. Two are real fail-open misclassifications: the shell runs the heredoc body, or a sed program taken from a variable, while the classifier reports `nonexec`. I deliberately did not build complete end-to-end bypass commands. Where I say "verified", I checked the classifier's output or the scrub output on harmless input, and I ran the corpus. The impact claims in the first two items are inferred from that.

Test setup: everything ran on a copy of the head tree in `/tmp/hc/repo` (bash 5.2). `/tmp/hc/cls.sh` sources the fence with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and prints `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class`.

All paths are under `/workspace/pr/head/`. Line numbers are in `.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` unless another file is named.

**Fail-open: the class is wrong while the body or program can run**

1. **The tokenizer misreads `$'...'` quoting (lines 240-241, 251; verified).** It treats `$'\''` as a plain single quote, so the following ` | sh ...'` becomes one quoted word, and the pipe and second command are never seen. Bash does pipe into it.
   - Repro: `bash /tmp/hc/cls.sh $'grep -h x - <<EOF $\'\\\'\' | sh #\'\nhello x\nEOF'` prints `nonexec`.
   - Running the same command with `tr a-z A-Z` in place of `sh` prints `HELLO X`, which proves the hidden pipe exists.
   - The contract says an unreadable header falls back to a full scan and a shell member means `interpreter`. Here only fence-verb body segments are kept; everything else in the body is dropped (see item 7).
2. **Unquoted `$var` words are accepted in allowlisted forms (lines 441-443 with the regex at 192; line 353 in general; verified).**
   - `sed -n $p <<EOF` → `nonexec`, because `$p` matches the print-only regex (the `$` address followed by `p`). Bash expands `$p` first, so `p=e` turns it into GNU sed's `e` command, which runs each body line as a shell command.
   - `sort $o <<EOF` → `nonexec`. If `$o` holds `--compress-program=…`, sort can run that program (inferred).
   - Words that are not literal should make the form `interpreter`.
3. **`yq --split-exp` / `yq -s` is allowed (lines 427-432; verified `nonexec`).** mikefarah yq writes one file per document, named by the expression, so it can create `x.sh` or `.git/hooks/*` without going through the executable-destination check (`_bdb_hd_exec_dest`).
4. **Writes through a duplicated file descriptor are not tracked (line 340; verified).** `exec 3>run.sh` followed by `cat <<EOF >&3` → `nonexec`. `>&N` is skipped, so the real target is never checked by `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` or `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`.
5. **Executable-destination path checks are not normalized (lines 313-322; verified).**
   - With PWD on PATH, `tee x` → `interpreter` but `tee ./x` → `nonexec`.
   - With `tools` on PATH, `./tools/x` and `tools//x` → `nonexec` while `tools/x` → `interpreter`.
6. **The executable-destination list misses some paths (lines 190-191; verified `nonexec`).** `.mcp.json` (starts MCP server commands), `.husky/pre-commit` and `~/.ssh/config` (ProxyCommand) are all treated as plain files.

**The body segment scan disagrees with "dangerous segments are still scanned"**

7. **Segments are dropped when the command word is not first (lines 538-570, 585-597; verified with the scrub output).** In a `tee notes.txt <<'EOF'` body:
   - `rm -rf build` and `x=1 rm -rf build` are kept.
   - `if true; then rm -rf build; fi`, `for …; do rm -rf build; done` and `2>/dev/null rm -rf build` are all dropped. `then`, `do`, `else` and leading redirections are not stripped.
   - The fence-verb list (lines 214-220) also leaves out verbs that rules reading `_cmd_match` depend on: `cp`, `mv`, `ln`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `tar`, redirects (FR-SZ/FR-SZ2) and `gh` (SP-1). Body text such as `cp a .claude/hooks/x` is dropped.
   - Together with items 1 and 2, this is how executed body content escapes the existing rules (inferred).
8. **The "full scan" fallback is weaker than the per-segment scan (verified via the corpus).** The `interpreter` path (lines 700-703) feeds the raw body to the old rules, which do not match `\rm …` (row D131 is allowed with the knob off). A body the shell actually runs gets less normalization than a body that is only written to a file.

**Other defects**

9. **"Turning it off only tightens" is false (line 732, header lines 125-126; verified).**
   - `run-corpus.sh --knob-off` gives `dangerous 136/142`: D122, D123, D127, D131, D136 and D141 block with the knob on but are allowed with it off.
   - With the knob on, the corpus is fully green: `benign 89/89 dangerous 142/142 residual 0/5`.
10. **Runtime is quadratic, which risks a hook-timeout fail-open (lines 232-285, called per line at 658/664; verified).** A 20 KB line before a heredoc takes 1.1 s; an 80 KB line takes 25 s. 3,000 lines of 85 characters take 4.7 s, against 0.08 s without `<<`. If Claude Code lets the command run when a hook times out, a large command gets past the fence (inferred).
11. **`set -u` is unsafe when IFS is unset (line 317; verified).** Sourcing `.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh` under `set -euo pipefail`, then `unset IFS` → `IFS: unbound variable`, and the caller exits. Without `set -u`, the function still leaves the caller with `IFS=""` where it was unset.

**Tests and the wrapper**

- `tests/unit/guard-yield.bats` fails every test with exit 127. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh` does not exist in either base or head, so the edited row (line 34) never reaches the classifier.
- Nothing in the tree sources `.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh`, so the wrapper has no test coverage.

**Checked and correct**

- The `BDB_LIB_ONLY` guard (line 762): executing the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` still blocks (rc=2).
- `<<-` tab stripping for the terminator, and a missing terminator falling back to a full scan.
- Two heredocs on one header line, and context carried over from earlier lines (`|`, `&&`, `\` at line end, `$(`, keywords).
- The knob defaulting to on.
- `sed -n -e` correctly classifies as `interpreter`.

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:250 — Fail-open in the heredoc header tokenizer: the quote handling does not recognise bash ANSI-C quoting `$'...'`, so `$'\''` is read as an ordinary single-quoted word that never closes and swallows the rest of the line, e.g. ` | sh #'`. `grep -h x - <<EOF $'\'' | sh #'` classifies as `nonexec` (verified; the same command with `| tr a-z A-Z` proves bash pipes into the second member), so a body piped into a shell is scanned only per segment instead of in full. The contract says an unreadable header must fall back to a full scan.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:441 — Fail-open: the allowlisted forms accept unexpanded `$var` words. `sed -n $p <<EOF` is `nonexec` because the literal text `$p` matches `_bdb_hd_re_sedp` (line 192, `$` address + `p`), but bash expands it first: `p=e` gives GNU sed's `e` command, which runs every body line as a shell command. `sort $o` is accepted the same way (`--compress-program=`). Any non-literal word in an allowlisted member should make the class `interpreter`.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:430 — The jq/yq allowlist only rejects in-place flags. mikefarah `yq -s/--split-exp` writes one file per document under an expression-chosen name (e.g. `x.sh`, `.git/hooks/pre-commit`) and still classifies as `nonexec` (verified), bypassing `_bdb_hd_exec_dest`.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:339 — Writes through a duplicated descriptor are skipped (`>&N` is `continue`d). In `exec 3>run.sh; cat <<EOF >&3` the real target is never checked against `_bdb_hd_exec_dest`/`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`, so the command is `nonexec` (verified). The exec-destination checks (lines ~313-322) also don't normalise paths: `tee ./x` or `tools//x` on a PATH dir is `nonexec` while `tee x`/`tools/x` is `interpreter`.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732 — The comment says "turning it off only tightens", but `tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh --knob-off` gives dangerous 136/142: rows D122, D123, D127, D131, D136 and D141 block with the classifier on and are allowed with it off. The off switch is a loosening, and the old full-scan path (used for `interpreter` bodies) doesn't normalise e.g. `\rm` the way the new per-segment scan does.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:590 — The per-segment body scan keeps a segment only when its first word is a fence verb. `then rm -rf …`, `do rm …` and `2>/dev/null rm …` segments are dropped, contradicting the header's "fence-verb segments are kept for the normal rules". Rules that match `cp`/`mv`/`ln`/`tee`/`sed -i`/redirects/`gh` are not in the kept-verb list (lines 214-220), so body text those rules used to see is now silently discarded.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — `--arg label "$label"` / `$label` (lines 380, 389) is a jq keyword under jq 1.6, still the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. The per-sprint jq fails to compile ("syntax error, unexpected label"), so under `set -e` every `derive` exits 3 (verified with jq 1.6; it works on 1.7.1). `write`, `mark`, the /loa Run line and the implement gate's deny-mode run position (derived_at never gets written) all silently degrade. Rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:324 — `breaker OPEN → HALTED` is a first-match rule applied on every `derive --write`, and every checkpoint `write` and `mark` runs one. After `/run-resume --force` (halt-resume.md step 5: "continue without reset") the breaker stays OPEN, so the very next checkpoint flips `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` back to HALTED while the run is actually progressing. `record-round` also exits 10 on any non-approved round because the breaker is "already OPEN".
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:527 — On a trip, `record-round` runs `atomic_update "$state_file" '.state = "HALTED"'`, and atomic_update builds from `{}` when the file is absent. With no `.run/state.json` (e.g. sprint-plan or an explicit `--state-file`), this creates a bare `{"state":"HALTED"}` run state with no run_id, branch or timestamps for run-preflight, the gate and /run-resume to trip over. It should skip when the file doesn't exist.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:78 — Cache-key fallback bug: GNU `stat -Lc` exits non-zero when any one of config/profiles.yaml/floor.yaml is missing. The BSD fallback `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'` then runs on GNU as `--file-system`: it prints filesystem block/inode counts, not the files' mtime/size, and that text becomes the cache id. Config edits are then served stale from `.run/effective-config.json` (verified: with floor.yaml absent, PL-5/PL-8 return the old profile's values). Detect the flavour of stat rather than chaining on failure, and stat only the files that exist.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61 — `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE` (and `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT`) are honoured unconditionally, while the same file bats-gates `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` and the SessionStart hooks deliberately gate their config seams (L7 CRIT-1). head/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh:141 — Fail-open regression: the fallback went from enabled to `false`. With no config, a missing profiles.yaml, or yq/jq absent (`_loa_pl_live` returns the fallback), danger-level enforcement is now off where base defaulted to on (`return 0 # Default to enabled`, `|| echo "true"`). The same applies to guardrails-orchestrator.sh:110 for input guardrails. Even if the `standard` default is meant to be false, tool or file failure should not silently disable a safety guard.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:132 — The per-task key is `.checkpoint.task`, but `run-checkpoint.sh read` trusts a task checkpoint only when that bead is already CLOSED (the "last closed bead", state-schemas.md). So the writes for task N+1 accumulate under task N's file. The summary's `task` and the reviewer's `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` lookup (reviewing-code SKILL.md:220) name the wrong bead, and the 20-file rotation (line 174) can delete a sprint's earlier beads before review. Each Write/Edit also now runs run-checkpoint.sh plus `br show` on the hot path.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193 — The warning still says "Session diff total" although the total is now per task/key. It's the line users and the review axis read.
head/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh:243 — The lint reports an ERROR when the class is empty and only the `## Agent Teams` heading remains (no marker), and says "run generate-constraints.sh". But `prune_optional_table` (generate-constraints.sh:169) is a no-op without the start marker, so the suggested fix never clears the error.
head/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh:188 — The prune awk exits 0 when it ends in state `head` (heading/table at EOF, or markers above the heading). The markers survive and the generator reports success instead of failing with code 3/4.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:320 — The "Exit code semantics" test (and line 257) now accepts exit 0 or 1 through `assert_no_errors_exit`, so it no longer checks that "exit 0 = all pass". A regression that turns every PASS into a WARN stays green.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:110 — Step 5 says to call record-round only on findings and reads as "exit 10, HALT" unconditionally. The Circuit Breaker section (line 132) says to run it after each review/audit and HALT only on exit 10. Pick one rule and state it as "on exit 10, HALT".
head/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md:52 — This says rtfm-testing "writes one new report per run and edits nothing", but rtfm-testing SKILL.md:55 declares `WRITE: grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/ (reports and baselines)`. The added write exception (validate-skill-capabilities.sh) is justified by prose that doesn't match the skill.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 19 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**What blocks merge:**
- **The new heredoc classifier fails open.** It is supposed to fall back to a full scan whenever it can't read a header, but I confirmed two cases on harmless input where it reports a command as safe ("nonexec") while the shell still runs the content:
  - It doesn't understand bash's `$'...'` quoting, so a ` | sh` after such a word is hidden from it.
  - It accepts unexpanded `$var` words: `sed -n $p` passes, but with `p=e` GNU sed runs every body line as a shell command.

  Smaller gaps:
  - `yq -s`/`--split-exp` can write to executable paths.
  - Writes through `>&3` aren't tracked.
  - Path checks aren't normalised: `./x` passes where `x` is caught.
  - The header comment says turning the classifier off "only tightens". In fact, the test corpus run with it off lets six dangerous rows through that it blocks when on.
- **`run-checkpoint.sh derive` breaks on jq 1.6.** It uses `$label` as a jq variable name, which jq 1.6 rejects as a keyword. jq 1.6 is still the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. I confirmed it exits 3 on 1.6 and works on 1.7.1. Checkpoint writes, `mark`, the /loa Run line and the deny-mode run position all quietly stop working.
- **The profile cache can go stale.** If any one of the three files it watches is missing (e.g. no `floor.yaml`), GNU `stat` fails and the BSD fallback returns filesystem block counts instead of the files' modification times. Config edits are then served from the old cache. I reproduced this through the profile-lib tests.
- **Guardrails can now be switched off by accident or on purpose:**
  - The profile library honours its `LOA_PROFILE_*` environment variables with no test-only gate, so an environment variable can now disable danger-level and input guardrails. Before, those read a fixed config path.
  - Both guards now fall back to "off" when the config, profiles file or jq/yq is missing; the base defaulted to on.

**Other defects:**
- After `/run-resume --force`, the circuit breaker stays OPEN and the next checkpoint flips the plan state back to HALTED.
- When the breaker trips with no `.run/state.json`, `record-round` creates a bare `{"state":"HALTED"}` file.
- The karpathy diff hook files each task's writes under the previously *closed* bead, so the reviewer looks up the wrong file. It also now runs `br show` on every Write/Edit.
- Lint and generator: the lint tells you to run the generator for a state the generator can't fix. The generator can report success without pruning. A lint self-test was loosened so it no longer checks "exit 0 = all pass".
- Docs contradict themselves on when to call `record-round` and on what rtfm-testing writes.

**What I couldn't run:** the PR snapshot holds only the changed files and lost the executable bits, so I tested a copy:
